summary: SL-109 gave ScanStore a "not listed" mark in bit 0x80 of the existing Flags byte. Append sets it on folders, SetChildren clears it, Flags() masks it, and the new NotListed(int) reads it. Scanner.ListRoot now appends the root right after the directory check. It shipped with one build, 984 tests passing (964 baseline plus 20 new, none edited), a 5M stopped-at-unlisted-peak Fact, and 40 real-data stops at validate with 0 mismatches. All three reruns (risk-spike, critique, code-review) were disposition rounds, not code rework. The real cost was one critique disposition (M1) marked accepted-fixed that was never built, and a rule-1 "class closed" claim that code review reopened.

payload.summary: SL-109 gave ScanStore a "not listed" mark in bit 0x80 of the existing Flags byte. Append sets it on folders, SetChildren clears it, Flags() masks it, and the new NotListed(int) reads it. Scanner.ListRoot now appends the root right after the directory check. It shipped with one build, 984 tests passing (964 baseline plus 20 new, none edited), a 5M stopped-at-unlisted-peak Fact, and 40 real-data stops at validate with 0 mismatches. All three reruns (risk-spike, critique, code-review) were disposition rounds, not code rework. The real cost was one critique disposition (M1) marked accepted-fixed that was never built, and a rule-1 "class closed" claim that code review reopened.
payload.estimate_error: Risk tier medium was right. The spike's no-go was real (a Stop in the root's listing left no root, 20/20) and was fixed by moving one call in Scanner.ListRoot. Size medium held for product code (ScanStore.cs, Scanner.cs, a comment in EntryKind.cs), built in one attempt. It under-counted the test and rules-tooling surface. The design declined rules to avoid harness cost. The composer then added two settled rules, and critique m1 plus obligation O-015 grew them into four widened patterns, a 97-row corpus (tests/bugs/SL-109-NotListedBitRuleCorpus.json), a PowerShell checker, and the rules harness plus RuleCases runs at build, code review and validate. The build changed 13 files. This is the same undercount lesson #388 describes. Size a slice that touches .taad/fitness.yaml by the validation it drags in, not by lines of product code.
what_went_wrong: Critique finding M1 was disposed `accepted-fixed` with the clause 'Assumption, unchecked: the hook can bring the app to that state'. Nothing was built for it. No obligation was raised: O-015 to O-021 cover critique m1, m3, m4, m5, m6, m7 and the review's m1, and none covers M1. The design export the builder received still carried filed_for_later #2. The builder had to declare a deviation, code review re-raised it, and a second disposition at code review overrode the first. Validate then measured the app half by hand in a scratch hook outside the tree. The ledger holds two opposite dispositions on one finding.

Rule 1 was declared a closed class through a 97-row corpus (O-015 discharged). Code review found four spelling families the corpus lacks: a using-alias type, an @-prefixed type name, `global ::` with spaces, and the complement mask `& ~0x7F` / `& ~127`. Lesson #446 already names alias and @identifier. Q-251, from an earlier slice, shows the same pattern of gaps found after a text-rule slice. The gaps were waived to SC-371 and the rule still claims the class.

Four of the six accepted-pending findings were waived at build (O-017 m4, O-019 m6, O-020 m7, O-021 review m1). Two of those were partly built anyway. The build already collects twice (Aggressive) and records GC.GetGCMemoryInfo().TotalCommittedBytes (m6/SC-369), and SetChildren's doc comment and docs/design/SL-109-not-listed.md already state the one-whole-registration invariant (m4/SC-368). So those backlog items describe work already in the tree.

m7 (the one-entry RootUnreadable result) was waived, and validate reports it as 'local NTFS cannot easily produce it'. The critique's fix used the existing guard seam (OverrideQueryError returns 5 at the root's first List call), which needs no special NTFS state. A new Scanner.Scan result shape therefore ships with no test of its own. It is carried only by SC-370 and was not run at validate.

The risk spike halted the slice on falsifier (h), which its own text called 'expected as Core stands (U-189)'. The same run had already validated the fixed variant (root appended first: 20/20 roots NotListed, 964/964 tests). The halt added a stage lap and a 'built anyway despite a no-go spike' entry but no information.

Figures in the tree disagree with the validated measurement. docs/design/SL-109-not-listed.md:70 composes ~755 MiB from a 64.9 MiB idle window, and NotListedBudgetTests.cs:20-22 uses U-001's ~106 MB window baseline. Validate measured the real published window at 66.1-66.3 MiB idle and at most 742.8 MiB peak. Code review noted the inconsistency as drift, but nobody reconciled it.

learned.lesson: In this loop `accepted-fixed` on a critique finding creates no obligation and does not edit the design export the builder receives. Only `accepted-pending` findings turn into O-numbers the build must discharge or waive. If a disposition needs work (a new case, a measurement, a design change), mark it accepted-pending. If its feasibility is 'assumed, unchecked', probe it before disposing.
learned.evidence: M1 accepted-fixed at critique #2 produced no obligation, while m1, m3, m4, m5, m6, m7 became O-015 to O-021. builds#231 and reviews#300 both record that the design still carries filed_for_later #2. Validate had to measure the app half by hand.

learned.lesson: The app half of a memory criterion can be reached without scanning anything. A scratch startup hook (DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS) builds the synthetic store in the real published exe and calls MainWindow.ShowOutcome with a Cancelled ScanResult. A stopped ending builds no tree (MainWindow.xaml.cs:606-607), so only the largest-files list and the outcome panel hold the store. The builder's belief that this needed a real ~4.9M-entry tree on disk or a new FsaWindowHook mode held only for an in-tree, repeatable case. Scratch proved it works. A later memory slice should plan the app measurement this way from the start.
learned.evidence: Validate measured 3 fresh processes with a 4,879,990-entry store and 60,000 marked folders: idle window 66.1-66.3 MiB, peak at most 742.8 MiB against 1,024. The hook ran outside the repo, and validate's row 'tree has a repeatable test of the app's own commit' is recorded as failed.

learned.lesson: Memory headroom is now known at the stopped-unlisted-peak shape. Store retained 637.1 MiB and peaked at 653.6 against 800 (about 146 MiB spare). Core test host 690.0 MiB. App at most 742.8 against 1,024 (about 281 MiB spare). The completed-shape FiveMillionEntriesFitTheMemoryBudget still retains 654.3-654.6 MiB, so the mark costs 0 B per entry. Bit 0x80 of Flags is now the last free bit. The next flag needs a byte column (the design estimates about 4.8 MiB at 5M entries, well inside the headroom) or Kind's free bits with masking across seven reads.
learned.evidence: NotListedBudgetTests output at build and validate. Baseline ScanStoreBudgetTests 654.6 MiB retained and 670.6 peak (build-check) versus 654.3 at validate. Design key decision 1.

learned.lesson: Lesson #131's Scanner facts are stale in two ways. Its line numbers (FolderDone at :137-166) now sit at Scanner.cs:368-408. Its sentence 'the root listing is read whole before any append' no longer holds for the root entry. ListRoot now calls AppendRoot at Scanner.cs:261, right after the directory check and before DecideLastAccess, the keep reopen and _reader.List. Only the root's children are still appended after its listing. Store Count is 0 only for a Stop in calls 1-2, a token cancelled before the scan, a Refused root, or a non-directory root. Any later scanner slice (pause/resume, read-ahead) must re-read ListRoot and FolderDone first.
learned.evidence: Build-check cites Scanner.cs:370-371 and :377; code review cites Scanner.cs:261; NotListedTests.AStopInTheRootsListingLeavesTheRootNotListed pins Count 0 for k<=2 and Count 1 with NotListed(0) for later calls.

learned.lesson: SetChildren is the folder's single, whole registration and it clears the mark for any count. This slice's sweep tree cannot catch a block-wise writer. Its largest folder is 2,000 entries, while U-197's prototype flushes in 100,000-entry blocks, and RollupOracle.Feed already calls SetChildren per child. The pause/resume slices of this epic (U-197, U-180) must either keep SetChildren for the last block only or add a separate commit call. They also need a sweep folder larger than one block, with an assertion that a cut between blocks still reads NotListed. The invariant is written only in SetChildren's doc comment and docs/design/SL-109-not-listed.md.
learned.evidence: Critique m4, waived to SC-368. RollupOracle.cs:65 per-child SetChildren. The U-197 evidence on 100,000-entry blocks. The sweep tree in NotListedTests uses a 2,000-name folder.

learned.lesson: For a slice that edits .taad/fitness.yaml, count the rules harness (harness.py --scenario all, 167 rows), RuleCases C-001 and C-003, and any corpus checker as three or more runs (build, code review, validate), not one. A text rule written to guard a silent defect draws spelling-class findings every time. Either word it as a tripwire for named spellings and let the runtime guard carry the claim (the Enum.GetValues<EntryFlags> assertion here), or budget a corpus built against lesson #446's checklist (alias, @identifier, global::, complement masks, numeric forms). Do not write 'closes the class'.
learned.evidence: Code-review m1 found 4 gaps against the 97-row corpus. Q-251 shows the same pattern in an earlier slice. The build ran the harness and RuleCases twice and review and validate ran them again, each time 167/167 and AGREE 18.

learned.lesson: Check what a waived obligation already built before ranking its backlog item. SC-368 (block-wise-writer invariant) and SC-369 (double GC collect and committed-bytes record) were waived at build, yet the tree already holds their output-only parts. SC-370 (RootUnreadable one-entry Fact) was waived although the critique's seam-based fix needs no special NTFS state. Read NotListedBudgetTests.cs and ScanStore.SetChildren's doc comment before opening SC-368 or SC-369.
learned.evidence: builds#231 deviation: 'collects twice ... which finding m6 asked for and the person waived to SC-369; both are output-only'. LEFT OPEN: the m4 invariant 'is stated in SetChildren's doc comment and docs/design/SL-109-not-listed.md only'. Validate: SC-370 'local NTFS cannot easily produce it'.

learned.lesson: The corpora and scripts under tests/bugs/*.ps1 are outside the solution, so `dotnet test` never runs them. SL-109-NotListedBitRule.Tests.ps1 guards rule 1 and ran only because build, review and validate each invoked it by hand. Q-249 and Q-253 already record that nothing re-runs SL-104's corpus or Mutants.ps1 after merge. A later slice that edits rule 1 in .taad/fitness.yaml must run it by hand. Do not count it as a regression guard.
learned.evidence: reviews#300: 'no test under tests/bugs or tests/window (outside the solution, so the suite never runs them)'. validations#133 lists it as a manual run with the engine's venv Python.

learned.lesson: A risk spike whose falsifier is already known to fire halts the slice without information. Falsifier (h), 'a Stop in the root's first listing leaves no root', was described in its own text as expected as Core stands (U-189). The spike halted, and the engine then recorded 'built anyway despite a no-go spike'. State a known-to-fire condition as a prerequisite and test the fixed variant in the same run, as this spike actually did (20/20 roots NotListed, 964/964 tests). Then the verdict reads go-with-prerequisite and not no-go.
learned.evidence: risk-spike #1 halted and #2 passed with 'built anyway'. spikes#118: root-first variant left 20/20 roots NotListed and the suite 964/964.

lessons_judged.why: The design built CancelAtAnyCallMarksExactlyTheFoldersNotCommitted on Scans.RunCancellingAt and the AfterFolder/guard.Calls oracle. Both reviewers and validate named that sweep as the main evidence, and mutants (SetChildren not clearing, root appended late) were killed by it.

FolderDone as the single exit and 'an aborted listing commits nothing' were load-bearing for the design's cut-folder reasoning and the SMB-stall spike. The lesson's line numbers (:137-166) and its 'root read whole before any append' are now stale; this slice moved the root append earlier (Scanner.cs:261).

Single-threaded DFS and a frozen store after Scan returns justified treating the listed-ahead shape as covered by construction (material: false) and scoping out cross-thread reads. Validate confirmed that no read-ahead reader exists.
The mark lives in Flags and touches no size or charge path. The recount test reused RollupOracle, which already follows ChargedSize, but nothing here changed how sums are read.
No counting site changed. Scanner.Credit and CorrectSizes were untouched; the tests only checked that CorrectSizes under marked folders leaves the mark alone.

The design cited it to decide against an opt-in Trait for the 5M Fact. The Fact runs in the default suite in the MemoryBudget collection with no Skip or Trait, so CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped is untouched. The suite went from 28 s at baseline to 37.7 s at code review, not attributed per test.

The design had the designer read CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped and TempTree's root seam first. The undercount it warns about recurred on the rules and corpus side: 13 files, a rule widened from 1 pattern to 4, 97 corpus rows.

The design filed the person-run network pass and stated no stop-safety claim on shares. Build and validate recorded Cancel on a stalled share and Network=SMB-LOOPBACK as not re-run because Scanner.cs changed. Q-259 confirms the TEST-NET-1 guard cannot stand in for it.

missed.what: M1's `accepted-fixed` disposition promised a case measuring the real App's commit at the 5M stopped shape through FsaWindowHook, and withdrew filed_for_later #2. It rested on an explicitly unchecked assumption that the hook can reach that state unattended. No obligation or design edit followed. A check of the disposition against the tree would have found that Core keeps the store private to Scanner.Run and that FsaWindowHook has no synthetic-store mode. The gate did not run (a sizing decision for a medium-risk, one-designer slice), and the disposition was model-answered.
missed.caught_by: code-review (builder's declared deviation first, then reviews#300 re-raised it); validate measured the app half by hand

missed.what: Critique m1 listed several spellings of the always-false 'bit tested against Flags() outside the store' defect but not a using-alias of EntryFlags (`using NL = ...EntryFlags;` then `(NL)0x80`), an @-prefixed type name, `global ::` with spaces, or the complement mask `((byte)Flags(e) & ~0x7F) != 0`. Lesson #446 already names alias and @identifier, so the critique's spelling checklist was incomplete. The builder's 97-row corpus then inherited the same gaps while claiming to close the class.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 1 (finding m1, waived to SC-371)

unknowns: Does the epic's pause/resume work (U-197's 100,000-entry block flushes, U-180) register a listing in blocks or call SetChildren per block? If it does, the 'SetChildren clears the mark' contract fails silently and needs a separate commit call or a kept mark. This must be settled before that slice is designed.

Does the real Scanner stopped at the unlisted 5M shape stay under 1 GiB inside the real window? Validate used a synthetic 4,879,990-entry store and left the pending stack's path strings and the top-level snapshot (a few tens of MB) unmeasured, against about 281 MiB spare. Nothing guards it in-tree.

Can the one-entry RootUnreadable result (root passed the directory check, first List call failed with a non-cancel error, nothing kept) be produced with the OverrideQueryError guard seam, as critique m7 proposed? Validate says local NTFS cannot easily produce it, and nobody ran the seam route.

Does a Stop on a real SMB share, or on Windows 10, still leave the cut folder NotListed? The go spike held 20/20 only on an SMBLibrary rig, Sandbox build 26100. The person-run network pass is stale because Scanner.cs changed, and the TEST-NET-1 guard is red at baseline (Q-259).

candidates.title: Reconcile criterion 7's app figure in the tree with validate's measurement, and decide whether it gets a guard
candidates.why: docs/design/SL-109-not-listed.md:70 composes ~755 MiB (690.0 test-host + 64.9 idle window) and calls the app half unmeasured. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/NotListedBudgetTests.cs:20-22 uses U-001's ~106 MB window baseline. Validate measured the real published window holding the 4,879,990-entry stopped store (60,000 folders marked), through a scratch DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS hook calling MainWindow.ShowOutcome with a Cancelled ScanResult. Idle was 66.1-66.3 MiB and peak at most 742.8 MiB against 1,024, over 3 fresh processes. That hook lives outside the repo, and validate's row 'tree has a repeatable test of the app's own commit' is recorded as failed. Scope: correct the two figures, then decide between a tests/window/FsaWindowHook mode with WindowCases.ps1 parity (needs a WindowMutants -Mutant All run per Q-114) and accepting the one-off measurement. If the validate-filed app-commit item already carries this, merge the two.
